high.title: Ringgit Retreats on Middle East Concerns
high.summary: The ringgit depreciated to 4.0930/4.0990 against the USD despite Malaysia's Q2 2026 GDP growth beating expectations at 5.8% versus the 5.3% consensus forecast. The stronger-than-expected GDP indicates economic resilience amid global trade uncertainties and US protectionist policies. Full-year GDP growth is projected to remain around 5%, signaling continued economic stability for Malaysian investors.

high.title: Bursa Higher at Close on Foreign Fund Inflows, Second Quarter GDP
high.summary: The FBM KLCI gained 9.26 points (0.54%) to close at 1,731.45, driven by foreign fund inflows and positive Q2 2026 GDP data. Softer inflation has strengthened consumer spending outlook, while the OPR maintained at 2.75% supports a stable financing environment for business expansion. This market performance reflects growing investor confidence in Malaysia's economic fundamentals.

high.title: Bursa ends higher on broad-based buying
high.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 8.43 points (0.49%) to close at 1,722.19, supported by returning foreign fund inflows and optimism ahead of Malaysia's Q2 GDP release expected to remain above 4%. Wall Street's overnight gains driven by softer US inflation and strong bank earnings further boosted sentiment, with expectations growing that the Fed may begin easing monetary policy later this year.

high.title: Ringgit rises as soft US data weighs on greenback
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0655/4.0710 against the USD at market open after the US PPI unexpectedly fell 0.3% MoM in June, pushing the US Dollar Index down 0.43% to 100.485. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh signalled no urgency to raise rates, providing broad support for emerging market currencies including the ringgit.

high.title: Ringgit firms as US rate hike expectations recede
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0710/4.0745 against the USD at market close, benefiting from softer-than-expected US CPI and PPI data for June and the Fed chair's remarks indicating no rush to raise interest rates. Asian currencies broadly firmed against the greenback, though the ringgit remained mostly lower against other major currencies.

high.title: Bursa ends lower, weighed by profit-taking in banking, energy stocks
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed down 6.18 points at 1,713.76, dragged by profit-taking in banking and energy sectors. Despite the weaker headline index, market breadth remained positive with healthcare, consumer and plantation stocks outperforming, signalling a shift to defensive plays amid geopolitical uncertainty. Turnover expanded to 4.07 billion units valued at RM2.84 billion.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher ahead of Q2 GDP estimate
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0740/4.0780 against the US dollar ahead of Malaysia's Q2 2026 advance GDP release on Friday. Economists forecast GDP growth above 5%, supported by E&E and commodity exports, though cautious consumer spending may temper the expansion. This data will be a key indicator for investor sentiment and monetary policy outlook.

high.title: Bursa gains on improved sentiment ahead of GDP data
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened higher with the FBM KLCI rising 3.15 points to 1,723.09, buoyed by a Wall Street rebound in semiconductor stocks and weaker-than-expected US June inflation data. The softer US CPI eased fears of further Fed rate hikes, pushing the US 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.587%. This positive external backdrop provided early uplift to Malaysian equities.

high.title: Energy, banking stocks lift Bursa
high.summary: The FBM KLCI surged 21.50 points (1.26%) to close at 1,719.94, driven by energy and banking stocks amid escalating US-Iran tensions and concerns over oil supply disruptions. Brent crude jumped to US$83 per barrel following Trump's declaration of a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. Bursa Malaysia outperformed regional peers due to its defensive sector composition and strength in commodity-linked stocks.

high.title: Bursa opens higher on healthcare, property buying
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened higher at 1,700.85 on healthcare and property buying interest, despite Wall Street declining due to escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions. Trump's declaration of a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz caused a spike in crude oil prices, with Brent crude rising to US$83 per barrel. This sets significant context for Malaysian energy-linked equities and broader market sentiment throughout the trading session.

medium.title: Trump Threatens to Increase Canadian Tariffs Over Wildfire Smoke Pollution
medium.summary: Trump threatened to increase tariffs on Canada over wildfire smoke pollution, citing 'willful negligence' and billions in costs to the US. Escalating US-Canada trade tensions could have broader implications for global trade sentiment and supply chains that affect Malaysian exporters. This adds to existing global trade uncertainty that Malaysian businesses and investors need to monitor.

medium.title: Bursa Opens Slightly Lower on Profit Taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened slightly lower due to profit-taking and a pullback in US semiconductor stocks, pressuring the local technology sector. However, optimism surrounding the official launch of the Large Scale Solar 6 (LSS6) programme is expected to cushion downside risks and drive buying interest in renewable energy and energy storage stocks. Malaysian investors should watch for sector rotation opportunities in the clean energy space.

medium.title: Ringgit Flat Against US Dollar, Higher Versus Major Currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit traded range-bound between RM4.06 and RM4.08 against the USD, with market focus on Malaysia's Q2 2026 GDP advance estimate and the Fed's interest rate stance. A rising US Dollar Index (DXY) at 100.763 points reflects continued hawkish Fed sentiment, which caps ringgit appreciation potential. Malaysian businesses with USD exposure should monitor Fed policy developments closely.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds on stronger investor appetite
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 4.30 points to 1,718.06 at the morning open, driven by improved global risk sentiment following softer US producer inflation data. Technology counters were highlighted as likely beneficiaries of selective buying, while broader market breadth showed losers outpacing gainers early in the session.

medium.title: Ringgit ends flat against US dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit closed flat at 4.0760/4.0805 against the USD as positive US CPI data was offset by concerns over China's slowing Q2 2026 GDP growth of 4.3%, down from 5% in Q1. Geopolitical risks in the Middle East, including renewed US-Iran tensions threatening Strait of Hormuz shipping, added to cautious trading sentiment.

medium.title: Ringgit ends lower against US dollar amid cautious sentiment
medium.summary: The ringgit weakened to 4.0760/4.0800 against the greenback as traders awaited US June CPI data, with consensus expecting headline inflation to moderate to 3.8%. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and potential disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz added to risk aversion, keeping crude oil prices elevated. These factors could influence Malaysia's trade and inflation outlook.

medium.title: Syahrul Azmir made new CEO of Rapid Bus
medium.summary: Rapid Bus has appointed Syahrul Azmir as its new CEO, bringing over 27 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, and transport sectors. The appointment coincides with Rapid Bus's push to expand electric bus deployment and improve service reliability across Rapid KL and Rapid Penang networks. This leadership change signals a strategic focus on operational transformation and sustainable public transport.
